assessment 2"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/medicinedepartment.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/blended-learning-bimonthly-assignment.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1st case:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/sreejaboga.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/is-online-e-log-book-to-discuss-our.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChest pain:epigastric region-may be in esophagus (Gerd)or pancreatitis, peptic ulcer, inferior wall MI\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAbdominal distension : hepatitis,cirrhosis hypoalbuminemia or renal failure or heart failure. In surgical point of view we can also consider peritonitis as he also have abdominal pain (site not mentioned), hollow viscus perforation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe is a known case of alcoholic so we can also think of hepatorenal syndrome.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe also have SOB which can be attributed to lung pathology or heart failure or renal failure which lead to pulmonary edema or pleural effusion causing SOB. He is also a smoker so it goes in favour of lung pathology. His chest X-ray showed pleural effusion. So that explains the crepts in systemic examination.His ABG also shows acidosis which can also cause SOB.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEvents:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECongenital bow leg deformity----\u0026gt; Alcohol \u0026amp; smoking (30 years)----\u0026gt; Abdominal pain \u0026amp; distention , SOB , chest pain , decreased urine output (3 days)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOUTCOMES:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUrine output increased , pedal edema and SOB decreased (Day-2)----\u0026gt;Altered sensorium (Day-3)----\u0026gt; Dialysis done (Day-4)----\u0026gt; Bilious vomiting (Day-5)----\u0026gt;Dialysis done (Day-6)----\u0026gt; Abdominal pain \u0026amp; vomitings subsided (Day-8)----\u0026gt;MHD for his renal failure ----\u0026gt; Patient died (Day-15)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFluid therapy in view of third space volume loss in acute pancreatitis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAntibiotics for pancreatitis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETramadol for pain management.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EZofer-for complaints of nausea and episodes of vomiting\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELasix-for ascitis and decreased urine output.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Nebulization because of his creptitations\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENBM\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOxygen for his decreased saturation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERules tube insertion\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2nd case:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/aakansharaj.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/55-year-old-male-with-anemia.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is a case of fever and going by the history we can suspect UTI or respiratory tract infection as there are chills and rigors. Further into the discussion we can also include tuberculosis,malignancy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETuberculosis is favoured by low grade intermittent fever,with productive cough with weight loss, loss of appetite.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient has generalised weakness,weight loss, chronic anemia which may include malignancy as the differential.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient also gives GI symptoms of vomiting, pain abdomen in right hypochondriac region where liver is present. This may also include hepatitis. Hepatitis is further supported by vomiting, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, weight loss.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETimeline of events:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol \u0026amp; smoking (35 years)----\u0026gt; Stopped alcohol (4 years)----\u0026gt; Fever , generalised weakness \u0026amp; anemia - 2 units blood transfusion (1.5 years)----\u0026gt; Stopped smoking (4 months)----\u0026gt; Low grade fever , generalized weakness , headache , neck pain , loss of appetite , weight loss (2 months)----\u0026gt; Cough \u0026amp; SOB (2 weeks) ----\u0026gt; Vomiting \u0026amp; pain abdomen (2 days).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOUTCOME:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESome symptomatic relief and referred to higher centre in need for oncologist.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPharmacological intervention:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAntibiotics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBlood transfusion\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological intervention:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPleural fluid analysis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EImaging -xray skull, HRCT chest\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESerum electrophoresis,sputum culture\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3rd case:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttp:\/\/nithishaavula.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/51-yr-old-male-with-hfref.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)pedal edema with abdominal distention with sob suggestive of right heart failure or renal failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB)etilogy of rt heart failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETimeline of events:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETobacco chewing (40 years) ----\u0026gt; Alcohol (10 years)----\u0026gt; DM (7 years) ----\u0026gt; HTN (5 years)----\u0026gt; 1st Episode GTCS (3 years) \u0026amp; AF with HFpEF ----\u0026gt; 2nd Episode GTCS (2 years)----\u0026gt; HFrEF \u0026amp; Anasarca (1 year) - (subsided with medication)----\u0026gt; Pedal edema (6 months) ----\u0026gt; Increased pedal edema , abdominal distention , SOB and decreased urine output (3 days)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOUTCOME:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESymptomatically releived and discharged.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPharmacological interventions:.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPreload reducers\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiuretics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAce inhibitors\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBeta blockers-Rate controlling agents\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAntiepileptics for known case of epilepsy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInsulin for glycemic control in diabetes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological interventions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESalt and fluid restriction\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4th case:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehttps:\/\/nairaditya97.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/31-yr-old-male-with-bl-pedal-edema-with.html?m=1\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHEART FAILURE (pedal edema , penile \u0026amp; scrotal swelling and SOB) :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMay be due to Alcohol causing wet beriberi\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAXONAL SENSORY POLYNEUROPATHY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMay be Alcohol induced\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETimeline of events\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlcohol \u0026amp; khaini (3 years) ----\u0026gt; Pins and needles (1 year) ----\u0026gt; Palpitations (8 months)----\u0026gt; PND (3 months) ----\u0026gt; Pedal edema and SOB (2 months)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;OUTCOME:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECompletly relieved of his symptoms as the wet beriberi resolved.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPharmacological interventions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)Lasix- to reduce edema\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2)Thiamine-nutritional supplementation for wet beri beri\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3)Telmisartan\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1)fluid and Salt font-size: 15px; text-align: center;\"\u003EThis is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"background-color: white; color: #757575; font-family: Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px;\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHere we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis history is of a 41 M, bus cleaner by occupation, which dates back to February when he came to our hospital with complaints of loss of appetite, dyspnea, fatigue which was present since 6 months I.e., since August.Patient was apparently asymptomatic before August of 2019 when he first started feeling weak and out of breath while doing his daily activities which hindered his routine, making him unable to do his work like he used to do. He also has lost weight of approximately 3-4 kgs which was known from loosening of his dresses since 4 months. There is history of fever 2 months after he started loosing weight .He also complained of body pains since 1 week prior to presentation and also fever, polyarthralgia and dry cough since\u0026nbsp; 4 days\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;He came to casualty with history of fever of low grade with chills and rigors which is intermittent type with no clinical variation since 4 days before presentation with 2 episodes of fall preceded by giddiness on the day of presentation.He had polyarthralgia involving B\/L knee joint, small joints of hand and foot, ankle, wrist.\u0026nbsp; After that his fever reduced but body pains reduced only by about half compared to his initial presentation and patient was discharged. Till 15 days back he doesn't record any new onset of symptoms. Now he came to the opd with complaints of cough since15 days which is productive with whitish sputum,\u0026nbsp; and no diurnal variation, and is associated with cold. He also complains of chest pain since a day, non radiating, squeezing type. No aggravating or relieving factors.patient gives no history of headache, blurring of vision, excessive sweating, palpitations, shortness of breath, syncopal attacks, no awakening from sleep to take lungful of air. He still have joint pains involving bilateral shoulder and small joints of foot and hand with early morning stiffness. There is joint space tenderness. Patient is an alcoholic for about 6 years and stopped drinking 3 years back.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt the time of presentation:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is afebrile, Bp-100\/60 mm Hg, PR-112 bpm, RR-20 cpm.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient has pallor, no icterus ,clubbing, cyanosis,lymphadenopathy,edema\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECvs:S1,S2 heard,\u0026nbsp; Loud S1, tachycardia present, no murmurs\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERs:BAE+, NVBS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMusculoskeletal system:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EJoint space\u0026nbsp; tenderness of ankle wrist and small joints of hands and feet.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere was both Active and Passive Limitation of Joint Movements with restricted range of movements (ROMs)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is ulnar deviation of the fingers and radial deviation of the metacarpals bones.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is piano key deformity of distal radioulnar joint.(Piano key deformity is due to subluxation of the distal radio ulnar joint)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECRP-Positive\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERA factor-negative\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EECG-showing PR segment depression\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; His history dates back to 2017 when he first developed shortness of breath where he couldn't even walk more than 20 steps (grade 3) and is associated with increased efforts to take air in, he also gives history of heavy bound palpitations. He gives negative history for pedal edema, cough,cold,fever, night sweats,weight loss at that time. And for his shortness of breath he first came to KIMS hospital and here they got to know that his ecg was abnormal (findings unknown) and they were referred to higher centres in view of need for cardiologist. They went to another hospital in Hyderabad where the cardiologist suggested an angiography. They agreed for it and the result came out to be blockade of three vessels to the heart according to patient's attendant words(patient's wife). For which he had undergone Coronary artery bypass grafting. Later the patient with his attenders repeatedly visited the hospital for follow up on doctors advice. He didn't show any worrisome problems until yesterday. He came to casualty yesterday evening with complaints of giddiness and nausea from 2 pm in the afternoon.This episode was sudden in onset and began after he had a heavy lunch. Patient's attendants also noticed he had profuse sweating at that time for which they got worried and consulted a local doctor and were told the giddiness was because of high blood pressure and patient was given Tab vertin. But the giddiness didn't subside so they decided to opt our hospital and while he was travelling to our hospital he gives history of 2 episodes of vomiting (non bilious,non projectile,non foul smelling, associated with food particles).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe has no history of ringing sensation in the ears, ear pain, any discharge from the ears or foreign body sensation in the ears. Patient gives a 3 year history of left sided hearing loss.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of headache,involuntary movements,Loss of consciousness.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of pain abdomen,loose stools,no bleeding per rectum.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of chestpain,palpitations, shortness of breath at the time of presentation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient had another episode of vomiting in the hospital with food particles as its contents.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe was diagnosed with hypertension at the time of his hospitalization for shortness of breath I.e 2 and half years back and he is on regular medication (Carvedilol).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient takes mixed diet, sleep is adequate,bladder movements are regular, no additictions. Patient has difficulty in passing stools.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient's mother was also diagnosed with Triple vessel disease at 72 years of age and was suggested CABG but she refused and opted for medical therapy.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt the time of presentation\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EO\/E: Patient was conscious, coherent,cooperative, well oriented.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVitals :BP-160\/90 mm Hg\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETab. Nicardia 10 mg po was given.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPR:95bpm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESpo2:98%\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGRBS:142 mg\/dl\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ES\/E :\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHINTS examination reveals-\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHorizontal bidirectional nystagmus and positive vertical skew with delayed saccades\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECNS : Higher mental functions are normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECranial nerves are intact.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPower :5\/5 in both UL and LL\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETone : normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EReflexes : exaggerated in both UL and LL\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPlantar - flexor\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESensory system : normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGait : Ataxic\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECVS : S1,S2 heard,no murmurs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERS : BAE +,NVBS,\u0026nbsp; no additional sounds.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EP\/A : soft, Non tender, no organomegaly, bowel sounds heard.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiagnosis - Class III NYHA with HFpEF with Triple Vessel Disease S\/P CABG with ?
